entities.summary: Cinematography is the art of motion picture photography, born out of the intersection of early photography, theater, and storytelling. The first motion pictures were created by the Lumière brothers in 1895, who captured the world's first film, 'Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory.' This innovation sparked a global movement, with the 1908 establishment of the Motion Picture Patents Company (MPPC) and the 1915 release of 'The Birth of a Nation,' which set the standard for narrative filmmaking. Cinematography has since evolved through the development of film stocks, camera techniques, and editing software, influencing art, culture, and society. The 1968 release of '2001: A Space Odyssey' by Stanley Kubrick revolutionized visual effects, while the 1995 release of 'Toy Story' marked the beginning of computer-generated imagery (CGI) in feature films. Cinematography continues to shape our understanding of the world, our emotions, and our experiences, as evident in the 2019 release of 'Parasite,' which won four Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director.
